name: Little Lunch
summary: A small food-enterprise identity that uses an approachable editorial story to connect the offer, the making and the practical plan.

palette.name: Text
palette.evidence: Dominant text-run color in source richSlides

typography.usage: Titles and short section openings; source slide 9 / ask.
Reading text, supporting labels and detailed explanations; source slide 9 / page.

recognitionRules: Use forest green and warm cream with rust food-story accents.
Pair Georgia narrative headings with Arial practical detail.
Keep the product idea separate from untested demand and operational assumptions.
Use a few generous food or making images with useful captions.

principles: Make the invitation warm and the practical details exact.
Use the identity’s sample as a rhythm and vocabulary reference, not as a factual project claim.
voice.sample: A small lunch, carefully made. Start with what goes on the table.
voice.sampleStatus: Original fictional brand copy authored for this guide, not a quotation or factual claim.
avoid: Avoid speaking for an entire community or implying confirmed attendance.
Avoid invented testimonials, performance claims and quotation attribution.
voice.secondaryExample: Come for the part that interests you; here is what to expect.
voice.cadence: Short opening, concrete follow-through; vary sentence length for explanation.

logoDirection: Use LITTLE LUNCH in Georgia with a modest Arial descriptor. A short curved underline may suggest a plate edge; avoid a complete restaurant badge.
invariants: Use forest green and warm cream with rust food-story accents.
Pair Georgia narrative headings with Arial practical detail.
Keep the product idea separate from untested demand and operational assumptions.
adaptations: Menus prioritize food names and practical details.
Business pages retain the same warmth while exposing cost and capacity assumptions.
Keep the full name with any new symbol until the audience can recognize it independently.

fonts.sourceFontDependency: Georgia is a separately licensed Microsoft/system font; not bundled.
Arial is a separately licensed Microsoft/system font; not bundled.

clearSpaceRule: Keep one half of the main wordmark cap height clear around the full silhouette, including its source-derived supporting device.

minimumSize.status: production minimum based on rendered 220/180px wordmark and 32/64px symbol inspection; verify again for unusual substrates
